summary: Compact batch synchronizer stall causing intermittent short-stream p99 cliffs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Glyph Analytics reports intermittent p99 latency spikes (short-stream requests) during sustained low-to-medium QPS. Spikes are brief (200-900ms extra tail) and show up as sharp p99 cliffs while p95 and median remain stable.

Impact:
- Affects user-facing interactive features for Glyph's product (dedicated cluster).
- Short-stream requests (<=64 tokens) occasionally hit p99 ~1.1s versus baseline ~180ms.
- Customer is seeing degraded UX for a subset of sessions; no 5xxs observed.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment for Glyph Analytics, prod us-east-1.
- Serving runtime v3.9.2 with continuous-batcher enabled and compact-window compaction on by default.
- Observed on nodes using NVIDIA A10 GPUs.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Load pattern: steady low-to-medium short-stream traffic (~40-120 rps from customer) with occasional short bursts.
2) Over the course of 2-10 minutes, an intermittent p99 cliff appears for short-stream responses across a subset of tenant-shards.
3) When the p99 cliff happens, traces show a ~150-700ms pause inside batch synchronizer/compaction path before flush proceeds.

Observed metrics and traces:
- p50 ~75ms, p95 ~210ms, p99 jumps to 900-1200ms during events.
- Batcher telemetry: flush latency spikes correlate with a "compact_window" syscall in the serving runtime.
- KV-cache miss rate increases marginally during events (~2-4%) but does not fully explain the magnitude of the tail.
- No CPU or memory saturation on the node; small CPU steal spikes (~5-8%) concurrent with events.

Logs (excerpt):
[2026-03-13T09:17:42.513Z] shard=12 tenant=glyph compact_window: start seq=48293
[2026-03-13T09:17:42.722Z] shard=12 tenant=glyph compact_window: acquired compaction-lock (worker=3)
[2026-03-13T09:17:42.980Z] shard=12 tenant=glyph compact_window: eviction pass took=258ms
[2026-03-13T09:17:43.015Z] shard=12 tenant=glyph batch_flush: flush initiated after compaction

Temporary workaround suggested: disable compact-window compaction on the affected tenant pool to avoid synchronized stall (can be done via tenant config toggle). This reduces p99 number of events but increases memory usage slightly.

Next steps: full root cause investigation assigned to SRE + serving-runtime engineers; implement jittered compaction and convert compaction lock to try-lock where possible; run canary before global rollout.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: timer/quantization alignment causes multiple worker threads to arrive at compaction at the same time, holding compaction-lock and stalling short-stream flushes. Evidence:
- Flamegraphs show a blocking region in batch_synchronizer::compact_window for impacted traces.
- Logs indicate repeated 'acquired compaction-lock' timestamps clustering to the same ~200ms bucket.
- Reproduced in staging by forcing compaction schedule alignment; when we introduce jitter the p99 cliffs disappear.
- Root cause seems to be a combination of: tight compaction window quantization + blocking eviction pass (non-yielding) + tenant heartbeat alignment that nudges tenant work into same tick.
Actions taken so far:
- Scoped staging test that injects 10-50ms randomized jitter into compaction schedule (PASS: no p99 spikes).
- Implemented a try-lock fallback prototype to avoid long blocking (proof-of-concept in branch).
- Draft PR with non-blocking compaction + jitter: PR #2487.
- Canary deployment started in us-east-1 (2 nodes) for Glyph's tenant pool at 2026-03-14T03:10Z.

comments: 2026-03-13T10:04Z - Support (Aisha): Triage complete. Notified SRE and assigned to Marcus. Customer provided request ids and sample traces. Asked to disable compaction as interim workaround.

2026-03-13T11:12Z - SRE (Marcus): Confirmed clustering of compaction-lock acquisitions in traces. Reproduced in staging by aligning compaction timer - p99 cliffs present. Added jitter in staging to validate - initial results promising.

2026-03-13T13:46Z - Eng (Lina Torres): Reviewed eviction code path. Eviction can take 150-350ms occasionally when scanning cold prefixes; adding per-tenant early exit reduces tail. Working on non-blocking eviction change set. See PR prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2487

2026-03-14T03:25Z - Support (Aisha): Canary deploy started for PR #2487 on two canary nodes in us-east-1 for Glyph tenant. Monitoring dashboards linked. Asked customer to report UX if they see further cliffs.

2026-03-14T04:12Z - SRE (Marcus): Canary metrics: p99 delta returned to baseline for canary nodes (before canary p99 spikes observed at ~950ms; after canary p99 ~210ms). No regressions in throughput or CPU.
2026-03-14T05:00Z - Customer (Glyph Ops): Confirmed reduction in tail for affected sessions. Asked for ETA on rollout to full pool and whether any config changes required on their side.

2026-03-14T05:15Z - Support (Aisha): Communicated rollout plan: gradual canary -> 25% -> 50% -> full pool over next 6 hours if metrics remain stable. No customer config changes required; recommended keeping compact-window enabled (fix is non-blocking).
resolution_notes:
Root cause: compaction scheduling quantization + blocking eviction pass created intermittent compaction-lock holds that delayed batch flushes for short-streams. Fix: PR #2487 implements randomized jitter for compaction windows, converts eviction pass to cooperative (yielding) behavior, and adds try-lock fallback to avoid blocking hot threads.

Rollout: Hotfix PR merged and deployed to canary 2026-03-14T03:10Z; gradual rollout to all Glyph dedicated nodes completed by 2026-03-14T09:00Z. Post-rollout monitoring: no further p99 cliffs observed in the 12h window; p99 returned to baseline.

Customer communication: Glyph Ops notified 2026-03-14T05:00Z and confirmed improvement. Follow-up: monitor for 48 hours and schedule a post-incident review to consider making jitter default for all tenants.
